newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines plans to import 650,000 tonnnes rice.
newsitem.headline: Philippines plans to import 650,000 tonnnes rice.

text.p: The Philippines plans to import up to 650,000 tonnes of rice before the third quarter, when local rice production is low, an official from the Agriculture Department told Reuters on Wednesday.

The government official said the Agriculture Department had asked for permission from the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council to allow state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) to import rice before the third quarter.
"We have to bring in between 500,000 and 650,000 tonnes of rice before the onset of the lean months," the official who requested not to be identified, said.

Early this month, Thai grains traders said Thailand sold 205,000 tonnes of rice to Manila at $300 per tonne. They said the first batch of 55,000 tonnes will be delivered between March and April and the remaining 150,000 tonnes will be shipped in May and June.
The Philippine Agriculture official confirmed the deal but declined to comment on the price.
As of February 7, the country's total rice stocks had reached 1.756 million tonnes, the NFA said.
